podcast.title: Reunion Discussions (2017)
podcast.body: In the summer of 2017, Chester Bennington was actively discussing a reunion with Gray Days. On July 18, 2017, he spoke with Sean Doudel, a band member he had known since they were teenagers, who reported that Chester "sounded great" during their conversation. "Chester was talking about a reunion with Gray Days, a band from his pre-Lincoln Park days in Arizona."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Chester Bennington's Former Band
podcast.body: Before relocating to Los Angeles and joining Zero/Hybrid Theory, Chester Bennington was the singer for a band called Grey Days in Phoenix. He left the group due to internal disagreements. "While in Phoenix, Chester became the singer of a band called Grey Days, but there were disagreements and Chester decided to move to LA"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Chester's Pre-Linkin Park Band
podcast.body: Gray Days was Chester Bennington's band during his formative years in Arizona, prior to him joining Linkin Park. "Chester was talking about a reunion with Gray Days, a band from his pre-Lincoln Park days in Arizona."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Local Sensation Without Major Label Interest
podcast.body: Gray Daze, which existed from late 1993 through 1998, became a genuine local sensation in Phoenix, opening for international acts. However, despite their popularity, they were unable to attract the interest of any major record labels. "Gray Days was a genuine local sensation, but for some reason they could not get any of the large record labels interested in what they were doing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Manager and Funding
podcast.body: The band was supported by their manager, who owned a local seafood restaurant, which presumably helped them with their endeavors, including releasing two indie albums. "helped along by their manager who ran a local seafood restaurant."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marriage and Career Frustration
xref.body: By 1998, a young Chester Bennington was married, despite both he and his wife being barely 20. Feeling completely frustrated with his lack of progress in the music industry, he quit his band Grey Daze and took a job as an assistant with a digital services company. "But by then, he was completely frustrated with his lack of progress in the music biz."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Upcoming Tour and Reunion Plans
xref.body: At the time of his death, Chester Bennington was preparing for a 29-date Linkin Park tour and had committed to a reunion with his former band, Grey Daze, after the tour concluded. He appeared happy, secure, and in excellent physical condition. "A 29-date Lincoln Park tour was about to start, and once that was over, he'd committed to joining Gray Days, the band he was in before Lincoln Park, for a reunion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
